subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram slash sessions still resolve to channel=(unknown), causing elevated allowFrom checks to fail on 2026.3.13

question: Should OpenClaw adopt, recreate, or defer the linked Telegram slash-session channel-resolution fix for elevated allowFrom diagnostics?
rationale: The issue is source-reproducible and security-sensitive, but the open candidates choose different fix shapes and neither has landed with live Telegram proof.

options.title: Adopt or recreate the narrow normalization fix
options.body: Use the mergeable candidate approach or a maintainer branch to make non-agent-scoped `telegram:slash:<id>` explain keys resolve to Telegram, then require regression and live Telegram proof.

options.title: Choose the static registry fallback
options.body: Use the registry-fallback shape only if maintainers want diagnostics to infer built-in channels without normalizing the session key, noting that the current candidate is conflicting.

options.title: Defer for live proof first
options.body: Leave the issue open and ask for a maintainer or contributor to provide live Telegram proof before selecting a repair.

recommendation.title: Adopt or recreate the narrow normalization fix
recommendation.body: Use the mergeable candidate approach or a maintainer branch to make non-agent-scoped `telegram:slash:<id>` explain keys resolve to Telegram, then require regression and live Telegram proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest combined history on `sandbox explain`, native command session targeting, and related command/config refactors.
